ac:layout-cell.p: We want the SQUARE app (are_tracker in bravo-agency-app) to follow the DK Jago app (digital_banking_app), the same way as the BFI Mobile assessment. This page compares the two. It lists the gaps and suggests an order of work. SQUARE shares one monorepo, one CI setup and 15 shared packages with GENFI, MyShaf and MY BISPRO, so about half of the findings here are the same on the GENFI page.

li.p: Three workflows in the repo print secrets, and one more exports the signing keystore. The SIT/UAT pipeline uploads the Android signing keystore and its password file as a downloadable artifact on every run: 156 runs so far, the last on 21 Oct 2026. See the Security items section. This is the first thing to fix.

Architecture is the biggest gap. No domain layer. Controllers call shared_data repositories directly and API models reach the screens. Features import each other freely (89 imports across 79 files; profile is imported by 35 files, maintain by 12).

The monorepo is a good start. Shared data packages per backend service, path dependencies, melos categories per app, and generated code kept out of the hand-written count. But the generated code is 8.7 times the hand-written code and is committed, and six near-identical auth clients live in shared_data.
Analytics: Event catalogue, typed events, one interface with Datadog fan-out. Turn RUM event processing on, or remove the SDK.
Logging is silently broken. Log.e writes at debug level under a warning threshold, so nothing reaches Datadog; RUM events are not processed either.
Testing is better than BFI. Controller tests are allowed and exist. But there is no coverage threshold, and no end-to-end tests.
App protection is missing. No RASP, no build registration. Pinning is only on in prod builds.
Decision already made: keep Riverpod. Copy Jago's layers, ports and analytics wrapper, not its bloc library.

p.strong: Where this app sits in the monorepo

ac:layout-cell.p: Effort: S = up to 1 sprint, M = 2–4 sprints, L = more than a quarter. Rows marked (shared) describe the whole monorepo.

td.p: Repo layout
Melos workspace. 4 apps, 49 module_* packages (features + shared), 110 library/* wrappers around pub.dev packages.

Melos workspace: 3 apps + 15 shared packages (shared). SQUARE is one package with 21 feature folders under lib/features. The apps are not members of the root workspace; melos categories list which shared packages each app uses.
Every feature lives in one package. 89 imports across 79 files; profile is imported by 35 files, maintain by 12. Nothing stops it.
L
Layering
data → domain ← presentation in every feature. Domain is pure Dart. Features talk through thin *_api contract packages. Rules are written down in .claude/rules.

Screen → controller (StateNotifier) → shared_data repository → HttpClient. No domain layer. Screens read repositories directly in loan_screen.dart:737 and collateral_asset_info_screen.dart:52. 41 screens and 57 controllers import the agency package; 66 lines in screens and controllers use *Response DTOs (e.g. feedback_confirmation_screen.dart:19). shared_data mostly maps network DTOs to "domain" models, which is a good base.
Business rules sit in controllers and screens. API changes reach the screens directly.
L
State management
bloc, with rules: no BuildContext or navigation inside blocs.
Riverpod 2.6 with the old StateNotifier API: 82 controllers, 103 static final provider. No global appRef (better than BFI). ref.watch inside callbacks: 0.
Keep Riverpod. Move to Notifier / AsyncNotifier.
M
Dependency injection
injectable + get_it. Each module exposes a micro-package. Wiring happens only in the app layer.
Riverpod providers. main.dart overrides HttpClient, NetworkConfig and the auth client per app through ProviderScope.overrides. Shared packages expose providers that throw until overridden.
Riverpod is fine as DI. The gap is ports: shared_data exposes concrete repositories, not interfaces, so nothing can be swapped or faked below the HttpClient.
M (comes with layering)
Analytics wrapper
AnalyticsPlatform interface. One fan-out sends each event to Datadog, Firebase and CleverTap. Events are typed classes.

A 37-line Analytics wrapper around Firebase only. 27 logEvent calls in 25 files, all with string-literal names, some built with interpolation. Calls are made from screen initState. User id is nikMarketing (employee NIK). Datadog RUM is a separate navigation observer, and its events are not processed (see the inventory page), so SQUARE is effectively unmonitored.
Event catalogue, typed events, one interface with Datadog fan-out. Turn RUM event processing on, or remove the SDK.
S
Logging and crashes
Monitoring fans out to Crashlytics and Datadog. PII is cleaned by jago_observability_sanitizer.dart.

Log.e creates a Datadog logger with a warning threshold and then logs at debug level, so nothing reaches Datadog. Crashlytics works and skips session, socket and timeout errors. Consent is hard-coded to granted. No PII cleaner. Crash user id is the employee NIK.
Fix the log level. Add a PII cleaner. Pick the user id on purpose.
S
Feature flags
Typed flag catalogue behind one FeatureFlagPlatform interface. Providers: Firebase Remote Config, Split.io, GrowthBook.

Typed freezed RemoteConfig with 23 fields, mapped by hand from SCREAMING_CASE keys in a 140-line repository. No setDefaults. One flag (FEATURE_FLAG_NON_REGISTERED_MAINTAIN) is a compile-time dart-define.
Generate the key mapping, move the dart-define flag into Remote Config.
S
Networking
dio adapter behind a client interface. 17 typed exception classes mapped to error messages.

core HttpClient (395 lines, dio) has no auth. SquareHttpClient, a 288-line decorator, refreshes the Keycloak token before every request, adds Authorization and x-marketing-id, and throws SessionExpiredException on 401 with no retry. The Keycloak repository has no single-flight guard, so parallel calls can refresh twice. Login is a direct password grant with the client secret, or a WebView code flow without PKCE. A second, separate sso package (AppAuth, PKCE) is used for the LORA handoff. Alice ships in release builds, disabled at runtime. (shared) Six near-identical auth decorators, 1,508 lines in total, exist across shared_data; only one of them retries after a refresh.
Interceptors with one refresh guard. Move Keycloak to the code flow with PKCE, so the secret leaves the app.
M
Security
Everspin Eversafe anti-tamper, CodeMix code protection on every prod build, each build registered, device fingerprint, screen-capture guard, certificate pinning.

Pinning only in prod builds; the SIT/UAT pipeline passes no fingerprint. Root check on (git fork), but the iOS alert has no button. No Play Integrity / App Attest. No screen-capture guard. CLIENT_SECRET (Keycloak) and GOOGLE_API_KEY are compiled into the binary; the same Google key serves Maps, Places and Firebase. R8 and shrinkResources on, plus --obfuscate, but proguard-rules.pro is missing. No allowBackup attribute, no network_security_config. Debug builds are signed with the release key. The SIT/UAT pipeline uploads the signing keystore as a downloadable artifact.
Stop uploading the keystore. Remove the client secret from the app. Pin everywhere. Add integrity checks. RASP needs a vendor.
S (fixes) / M (RASP, needs vendor)
Design system
module_design_library: tokens generated from a Figma export, brand and theme switching, Widgetbook published to GitLab Pages.

bfi_design_system_1 (ds_1) from frontend-mobile-ui, imported in 195 files. BfiColors 746 uses, BfiText 536. Raw styling remains: 46 TextStyle(, 10 TextButton(, 20 Colors. The monorepo ui_theme is not used. (shared) Four design systems are in use across the repo: ds_1, ds_2, ds_3 and ui_theme.
ds_1 is the oldest of the three design systems. Plan the move to ds_3 with GENFI. No Widgetbook.
M
Testing
About 5,288 test files. Coverage gate on changed files per module. End-to-end tests with Appium + Cucumber on BrowserStack.

135 test files: 854 widget tests and 394 unit tests. 71 screen tests, 9 controller tests, 6 repository tests. No integration or end-to-end tests. No coverage threshold. (shared) Coverage is computed for the whole package and posted as a PR comment with continue-on-error. collab_form has one empty placeholder test; sso, integrity and the pinning fork have none.
Coverage gate on changed files. End-to-end tests for visit report, lead submission and company submission.
M
Lint and guardrails
custom_lint rules, Danger bot, checks for generated files and package use, .claude/rules (14 files) and an mr-review skill.

(shared) Three lint sets: a 1,176-line strict_lint.yaml at the root, very_good_analysis in shared packages, flutter_lints in agent_tools. flutter analyze --fatal-infos in CI. pubghost dead-code check, but dead code and dead translations are allowed. No custom_lint, no architecture rules. Review bots: Copilot code review and a label-triggered Atlas webhook. copilot-instructions.md exists; no .claude/rules.
One lint set. No architecture checks.
S
CI/CD
See the next section.
(shared) GitHub Actions, 31 workflow files on master, 5 disabled. See the next section.
See the next section.
M

ac:layout-cell.p: SQUARE's pipelines live in the repo with the other three apps. Manual dispatch with environment sit or uat: APK + IPA to Firebase App Distribution (WIF). The pipeline uploads keystore.jks and keystore.properties as an artifact (156 runs). Trunk push builds a dev APK.

td.p: Trigger
Version tag, trigger branches, or manual on master.
Manual dispatch with inputs tag, version and a distribution flag (are-tracker-prod-deployment.yml). The branch filter on the dispatch trigger has no effect.
OK.
Toolchain
Flutter version pinned in one place (mise, CI image).
(shared) Flutter 3.35.0 copied by hand into 37 places. No .fvmrc or mise file. Java 11 and 17, Android SDK 33, 35 and 36, and three macOS runner labels are mixed across workflows.
Pin one version in one file (mise.toml or .fvmrc) and read it everywhere. Align Java, SDK and Xcode.
Version and build number
X.Y.Z+W from the tag. Build number from a CI counter.
pubspec.yaml fixed at 1.0.0+1. Typed by the operator and written into pubspec.yaml. No CI counter. Non-prod builds are always +1.
Use a CI counter so the build number always goes up.
Config
dart tools/env.dart writes config per environment. Firebase files are injected.
31, including CLIENT_SECRET, DOCUMENT_API_SECRET, MAPS_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY and the SSO and LORA URLs. Firebase config files are decoded from secrets.
OK. Review which defines are secrets that end up in the binary.
Build
flutter build appbundle, unsigned. iOS through fastlane.
AAB or APK (by flag) with --obfuscate --split-debug-info; iOS through xcodebuild.
Consider fastlane + match for iOS signing.
Code protection
CodeMix on the unsigned bundle, then zipalign, then apksigner.
R8 and shrinkResources on in build.gradle; proguard-rules.pro is missing. No protection step in the pipeline.
Add the rules file. Choose a RASP vendor.
Approval
Prod pipeline lives in a separate repository with its own access.
A job step (trstringer/manual-approval, 2 of 9 named people, using GH_PAT). The _build variant has no approval.
Protect the prod environment with required reviewers so every workflow that uses prod secrets needs approval.
Signing
Prod keystore only in the prod pipeline repo.
Keystore and certificates as base64 secrets, decoded at build time. The SIT/UAT pipeline then uploads the keystore as an artifact.
Acceptable once the artifact upload is gone and the environment is protected.
Distribution
Play internal track (script). TestFlight through fastlane.
Play internal track, or APK to Firebase App Distribution. TestFlight, or ad-hoc IPA to Firebase.
OK.
Post-build
Eversafe build registration (forgery tracking).
Symbols to Crashlytics (paths correct) and Datadog (no --version, so symbols may not match the build).
Fix the symbol paths. Add registration once a RASP vendor is chosen.
PR checks
Lint (+ custom rules), format, generated files, package rules, tests with random order, coverage on changed files, Danger.

(shared) Format, analyze, pubghost, tests, coverage comment. Runs only when *.dart files change: a PR that touches only .github/**, pubspec.yaml, Gradle or iOS files runs no checks. No coverage threshold. No test randomisation. No generated-files check. Conventional commit titles are asked for in the PR template but not enforced.
Run checks on every PR. Add a coverage gate on changed files and a generated-code check.
Release
Tag from the release branch.
(shared) tag-release-pipeline runs standard-version as bfibravo-bot with a PAT; the app is picked by matching text in the tag name. Only master exists; no release branches.
OK, but the tag-to-app matching is fragile (any tag containing "are" goes to are_tracker).

ac:layout-cell.h3: 1. Workflows that print or export secrets (urgent)
ac:layout-cell.p: Three workflows in this repo echo secrets through sed 's/./& /g', which puts a space between every character. GitHub hides a secret in logs only when the exact value appears, so the spaced-out value is readable by anyone who can open the run log. The same pattern was found in bravo-customer-app on 9 Oct 2026.

ac:layout-cell.p: What this means for SQUARE. The SIT/UAT pipeline (are-tracker-deploy-tag-cd-pipeline.yml, lines 88-95) uploads keystore.jks and keystore.properties as the artifact android-keystore-files, kept for one day. Anyone with read access to the repo can download the signing key and its password while the artifact exists. The workflow has run 156 times; the latest run was 21 Oct 2026.

The *_ro_tools environments belong to the RO Tools app, which moved to its own repo (branch archived/ro_tools, tags *-rotools). The secrets in those environments may still be the live ones for myBRO. Run history was checked through the GitHub API; no log was opened.

li.p: Delete test.yaml and debugger.yaml from master. Delete the "Reveal secret" step from the convent SIT pipeline and the keystore upload step from the SQUARE pipeline.
Rotate the SQUARE upload key with Google Play (Play App Signing lets you reset the upload key). It has been downloadable after 156 runs.

Rotate SSH_PRIVATE_KEY, BRAVO_GCP_SA_KEY and KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET in every environment that debugger.yaml names, and the prod keystore password. They were exposed to anyone who could run the workflow, and that is the safe default.

Add required reviewers to the four prod environments (agency_prod_agent_tools, agency_prod_are_tracker, sharia_prod_myshaf, sharia_prod_mybispro) and to prod_ro_tools, so no workflow can use prod secrets without approval. (Not verified: the current rules could not be read from this session.)
Add a CI check that fails any workflow which echoes secrets.* or uploads a keystore, and run it on PRs that change .github/**.
Check the other mobile repo, bravo-ro-tools-apps, for the same files.

Prod builds without environment protection (not verified). The approval is a workflow step, not an environment rule, and are-tracker-prod-deployment-build.yml builds a prod-signed APK and IPA with no approval. The environment settings could not be read from this session.
The Keycloak client secret is compiled into the app. Anyone can extract it. Move to the authorization-code flow with PKCE and treat the current secret as public.
Pinning is off in SIT and UAT builds, because the pipeline does not pass SHA_256_FINGERPRINT.
No device integrity check (Play Integrity / App Attest). The shared integrity package exists but SQUARE does not use it.
One Google API key serves Maps, Places and Firebase, and is compiled in. Split the keys and restrict each in Google Cloud.
proguard-rules.pro is referenced by build.gradle but not in the repo. Check what the release build really applies.
Datadog RUM event processing is set to NONE for both SQUARE RUM apps, so production errors and sessions are not visible.
The crash user id is the employee NIK. Treat it as personal data.
Tracking consent for Datadog is hard-coded to granted in main.dart (all three apps). Tie it to a real consent setting.
Secrets are interpolated straight into run: commands in several workflows, and inputs are used unquoted in shell. Pass them through env: instead.

Every third-party action is pinned by tag, and fjogeleit/yaml-update-action by the main branch (22 uses). The reusable update-graphify workflow runs from bfi-base-template@master with secrets: inherit. Pin by SHA.
Most workflows run with the default token permissions; only the WIF jobs set permissions: explicitly.

li.p: Who owns this plan? The squad that owns are_tracker (Agency), with a named tech lead. The shared plans (security, CI/CD, networking, lint, repo layout, design system) need one owner across the four apps in the repo.
RASP vendor and budget. The decision should cover bravo-customer-app, bravo-agency-app and bravo-ro-tools-apps together.
Coverage threshold. What number for changed files? A suggested start is 70%, raised over time.
Generated code. 291,420 generated lines in shared_data are committed. Generate in CI instead, or split the largest models?
Keycloak: can the backend team enable the authorization-code flow with PKCE for the SQUARE client, so the secret can be removed from the app?
Who owns Datadog for SQUARE? RUM is wired but not processed, and the Datadog subscription is mentioned as uncertain in code comments.
